gloss: back fat (pork fat used as a ramen topping)

definitions.explanation: Fat from the back of a pig, commonly used as a rich topping in ramen. It melts into the broth to add creaminess and depth.

examples.japanese: {背脂|せあぶら}たっぷりのラーメンが{好|す}きだ。
examples.english: I like ramen with lots of back fat.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}は{背脂|せあぶら}の{量|りょう}を{選|えら}べる。
examples.english: At this shop, you can choose the amount of back fat.

examples.japanese: {背脂|せあぶら}を{加|くわ}えると、スープに{濃厚|のうこう}なコクが{出|で}る。
examples.english: Adding back fat gives the soup a rich depth of flavor.

notes:
Pork back fat, widely used as a topping in Japanese ramen. It is typically rendered or chopped and scattered over the surface of the broth, where it melts and adds richness.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {背脂|せあぶら}たっぷり (loaded with back fat)
- {背脂|せあぶら}チャッチャ{系|けい} (back-fat-drizzled style ramen)
- {背脂|せあぶら}を{乗|の}せる (top with back fat)

Particularly associated with {燕三条|つばめさんじょう} ramen from Niigata and certain Tokyo-style ramen shops. Some shops let customers specify the amount: {少|すく}なめ (light), {普通|ふつう} (normal), or {多|おお}め (extra).
